BiblicalUsage: Naka means to smite or drive away, and its only occurrence is a scornful word about the lowly. In Job 30:8 the children of fools, children of base men, are described as viler than the earth, smitten down below the standing of men.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the verse is Job's complaint, not God's verdict, because Job is saying how the world treats the lowly; the smitten are not vile to God, even when men call them so.
